content.text:
I submitted **index 0** (Sb fraction 0.082, the La-rich end of the line) as the best composition. Its EQE was 0.0153%, which is very small; it was the only one of my five samples with a clear signal.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.082 | **0.0153** |
| 4 | 0.117 | 0.0002 |
| 14 | 0.308 | −0.0003 |
| 20 | 0.478 | −0.0005 |
| 25 | 0.618 | −0.0014 |

- **Model predictions:**
  - The two stable La antimonates, La3SbO7 and LaSbO4, are predicted to have band gaps of about 4.3–4.4 eV. That is too wide to absorb the 2.7 eV light used here, and the compositions near them gave essentially zero EQE.
  - La3Sb5O12 looked like the best bet: it is stable, with a predicted gap of 2.26 eV, at an Sb fraction of about 0.625. Its composition (index 25) gave no EQE, though, and its XRD did not match that phase.
- **XRD:** neither diffraction pattern (indices 25 and 5) matched any known La–Sb–O phase well, so I can't say which phase is behind the signal at index 0.
- **Uncertainty:**
  - The best point sits at the edge of the line, and index 4 (Sb 0.117) had already dropped to about zero. I never measured indices 1–3, so a slightly better composition between 0.08 and 0.11 could have been missed.
  - The Gaussian-process suggestion pointed to index 8. I spent the last measurement on index 4 instead, because it was closer to the only working sample.

All 5 EQE measurements were used; 3 of the 5 XRD measurements were left unused.
